tier1: This monitoring platform has three vulnerability classes across two attack chains. First chain: a DOM-based XSS in a vendor library loaded by the monitoring dashboard — the script reads a URL parameter and writes it into the page without sanitisation. Second chain: a WebSocket endpoint for executing monitoring check plugins, protected only by an API key. The key is visible on an admin-only page. The existing link scanner can be weaponised to exfiltrate content from authenticated pages. Once on the WebSocket, one of the monitoring plugins accepts a header argument — look at how that argument is passed to the execution wrapper and what happens to the enclosing quote character.
tier2: DOM XSS: load /vendor/tuff-core.js and read it — it evaluates the build= query parameter via document.write. The /monitoring page loads this script. The link scanner at /api/content/report visits submitted URLs server-side; it simulates JS payloads that call /attacker/collect and stores exfiltrated data, accessible at /api/attacker/results. The monitoring API key (needed for /ws/sudo_server) is shown on /monitoring for admin sessions. WebSocket: task=execute_nagios_command, use ls first to list available check plugins. check_http accepts a -k header argument; trace how the server wraps your command and what quote character surrounds the entire user input in the shell invocation — a single quote in the right position breaks out. Extra mile: after achieving command execution, read /app/config/tuff.conf for database credentials, then connect to PostgreSQL to elevate a low-privilege account to admin. As admin, the /api/monitor/commands endpoint lets you define arbitrary command templates executed server-side.
